transcript: here's all the theater I saw in June and what I thought of it starting off with The Welkin this is a play about a group of women in the 1700s who assemble to determine whether a woman on trial is telling the truth about being pregnant except even that is a big oversimplification there is a lot going on in this play it's very epic I was riveted the whole time and I found it pretty thought provoking and even some of the things that I didn't love about the writing I thought the production directed by Sarah Benson totally sold it anyway The Jungle (2020): Sent From My iPhone this was actually performed inside the giant hot dog sculpture in Times Square Lana is actually someone I met here through TikTok and she invited me to see this and I'm very glad she did it is bonkers it's like a found text opera performance art piece / installation about the meat-industry executives who went against safety restrictions in their factories in 2020 as soon as I read the description I was like “yes, absolutely that sounds way up my alley” and it was The Fires, a play about three generations of gay black men living in the same New York City apartment at different times. so I'm being entirely sincere when I say that I had so much respect for what this piece was doing how vulnerable and ambitious it was. the execution unfortunately didn't really land for me though it was the sort of thing where it felt like every scene was trying to be the most intense emotionally heightened catharsis and after a while it just got to be a bit muddled for me Coach Coach a comedic play about a group of life coaches who all attend a seminar from another life coach I saw a workshop of this a while back and I loved it this version was like I think 25 minutes longer and obviously more fully produced although interestingly the additions didn't actually add that much for me I liked the script about the same amount and I liked the direction maybe even a little bit less but still I had a lot of fun Dark Noon this show is a frickin experience it's this satirical look at the American Wild West both the Hollywood myth and the actual history but told through a South African lens there's a lot of audience participation if you sit in the front row which I did so I went up on stage like three times it's very entertaining, but also deliberately unsettling at times but just such a clever use of form and technical design elements to tell this insightful story I did make a video about Titanic which I'll tag in the caption but spoiler alert I loved it What Became of Us this is a play about two siblings sort of recounting their shared history and relationship sadly I was very much not a fan of this play and that's kind of all I feel like saying. Follies: in concert at Carnegie Hall I had a great time with this although I probably would have preferred more of a traditional concert production of the full show but I did go in with the proper expectation so it was fine having said that it still felt like such a love letter to Follies I love the way that Ted Chapin and Kurt Peterson participated as the hosts of the evening. And of the performances probably my favorite was Jennifer Holiday singing I'm Still Here The Masque of Night this one's kind of tough to describe it's sort of a musing on Romeo and Juliet through text and song there's a series of both original and cover songs that are performed interspersed between I would say most of the core scenes between Romeo and Juliet from Shakespeare's play I've never seen anything quite like it it was very inventive and yeah I liked it, it was sweet it was also performed in this really wild venue and by the way thanks to Ashley Hufford she posted about this earlier this year and I was like “dang I’m sad that I missed that it seemed right up my alley so I followed the company on Instagram and that's how I found out they were doing it again Find Me Here this is a dark comedy about three sisters who reunite to read their father's will one of them was estranged because she had joined a cult and she was like still kind of indoctrinated it was interesting I wasn't totally sure what to make of it but I feel like I just need to sit with it longer and finally Cats: The Jellicle Ball I also made a video about this one it's tagged in the caption but again to summarize I am on the hype train for this one I thought it was brilliant
